food.dish: hot roast beef, meatloaf and haluski
food.w: Family-run 1951 Bloomfield institution on Baum Blvd, named Pittsburgh Magazine's best diner — Greek-inflected diner classics like hot roast beef, meatloaf, honey-dipped fried chicken and haluski, open late Wednesday through Saturday. Cash only.
North Oakland bar from the Legume team where light-as-air pierogi and a cult bar burger share the menu with French-bistro plates — a Post-Gazette pierogi-project favorite and an Infatuation pick.
Swissvale corner tavern since the late 1940s and home of the 27-inch 'Battleship' hoagie stacked on bread baked in-house (also Torpedo and Destroyer sizes) — City Paper's Best Hoagie. Cash only.

Garfield pizza-and-sub shop beloved for giant hoagies and one of the city's best vegan-friendly menus — seitan wings, soy-cheese pies and locally sourced ingredients alongside the classic steak hoagie.

food.dish: crêpe-thin banana hotcakes and Lyonnaise potatoes
food.w: The Strip's cash-only griddle famous for crisp-edged, crêpe-thin banana or blueberry hotcakes and Lyonnaise potatoes — President Obama ate here, and it's a Pittsburgh breakfast rite. Cash only.
Since 1950, the Strip District's line-out-the-door breakfast institution — huge skillets, hotcakes and eggs off a busy open griddle in the heart of the market district. Cash only.
Old-school Strip District sub counter whose signature 'Big Nate' piles grilled steak and chicken with provolone and onions — a NextPittsburgh best-sandwich pick.
Woman-owned Strip District diner featured on Guy Fieri's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives — legendary haluski, big breakfasts and the Haluski melt. Cash-friendly comfort cooking.
